messages:
maria: Quick sync — I prototyped a 'tombstone sidecar + transfer-token' handoff for prefixes. Idea: instead of shipping full KV or relying on a lease handshake, the old owner emits a compact, append-only sidecar file with recent tombstones + a transfer token. New owner pulls sidecar and verifies token before accepting reads. Wanted to surface tradeoffs and get feedback.

jonathan: Interesting. How is token different from our existing manifest_v/op_id approach?

maria: Token is ephemeral and tied to a specific transfer snapshot (sha256(prefix || seq || epoch)). It's verified by the control plane to prevent split-brain handoffs. Manifest_v is still useful for global placement, but token lets us avoid synchronous fencing RPCs during move.

lee: Concern: sidecar persistence size under heavy churn. If a hot prefix has lots of deletes, sidecar could grow quickly and blow memory when pulled. Any compaction plan?

maria: Sidecar uses delta-encoding and time-windowed retention: only tombstones within the last T seconds (configurable, default 30s) are kept. We also cap by byte-size and index by sequence so new owner can rehydrate incremental tail. For very hot prefixes we fall back to a forced synchronous routing to old owner.

alex: How do we ensure correctness during concurrent compaction on old node? If compaction reorders tombstones and the sidecar was emitted before compaction finishes, new owner may miss a deletion.

maria: We attach a post-compaction watermark to sidecar: sidecar contains (tail_seq, compacted_until_seq). New owner applies sidecar only if compacted_until_seq <= observed local seq or else requests a compact-resync. The control plane will reject token issuance until compaction quiesces for that prefix.

jonathan: That's adding coupling between compaction and control plane. Could increase handoff latency. Do we have metrics to bound that?

lee: Also eviction edge-case: old owner may have evicted actual key payloads but kept sidecar. If new owner gets sidecar saying key deleted but doesn't have the payload or tombstone in local storage, how do we avoid stale reads?

maria: New owner must consult sidecar first: if sidecar indicates deleted -> return tombstone. If sidecar says missing and new owner has no local payload -> we conservatively consult the old owner via a short-lived RPC (transfer-verify). To limit RPCs we batch verify requests and backpressure on the prefill pipeline.

alex: Can we instead ship a tiny persistent bloom that encodes recent deletes (like 4KB) with the sidecar? Then new owner can make probabilistic decisions locally and only call back on 'maybe' hits. That avoids many RPCs.

maria: Yup, planned. The sidecar will always include a delete-bloom plus a small head snapshot (first N key hashes). Bloom false-positive rate tuned to <1%.

jonathan: How does this affect streaming reads and cursors? If a client holds a cursor and the prefix moves, cursor expects monotonic progression. Do we migrate the cursor state?

lee: My vote: don't migrate long-lived cursors transparently. Return a cursor-moved error with a hint to reestablish (cursor_token + manifest_v). Simpler and safe.

maria: Agreed. We'll implement a 'cursor_reacquire' code that includes transfer-token; the client can retry. For short polling clients we'll avoid retries by allowing a micro-grace window (~5s) where both owners accept the cursor token.

alex: Observability: we should emit three counters per handoff: sidecar_size_bytes, transfer_rpc_fallsback_count, and handoff_latency_ms. Also a histogram of stale-read-detections which triggers a high-severity alarm if >0.1% for 5m.

jonathan: Tests: (1) unit for token verification and sidecar compact/resync logic; (2) integ chaos: trigger move while compaction & eviction runs, assert no read returns deleted-then-present or present-then-deleted anomalies; (3) canary with proportional traffic and checksum probes.

maria: I sketched the checksum probe: pick 200 random keys from prefix head, compute xxhash64 fingerprint on old & new owner after handoff; if mismatch -> capture traces and increment counter. Cheap and reliable.

ops-bot: Created canary ticket: KC-2287. Chaos window scheduled 2025-11-02T02:00:00Z. Please attach rollback steps.

lee: Action items: (1) I'll own the bloom tuning and batching RPCs; (2) Jonathan, you own checksum probe + test harness; (3) Alex, add metrics & alerting; Maria, flesh out control-plane token issuance policy and sidecar proto.

maria: I'll post the sidecar proto + README to the repo in a WIP branch: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv-sidecar-transfer/tree/wip-sidecar-proto. Logs from local run:
```
[2025-09-30T09:01:04Z] sidecar_emit prefix=acct:42 size=4096 bloom_fp=0.008 seq_tail=8921 compacted_until=8918 token=sha256:ab12...
[2025-09-30T09:01:05Z] transfer_verify prefix=acct:42 token=sha256:ab12... -> accepted
[2025-09-30T09:01:05Z] node-9 prefill_started prefix=acct:42
[2025-09-30T09:01:06Z] node-9 applied_sidecar prefix=acct:42 deleted=7 maybe_deleted=1 verify_rpc=0
```

jonathan: Nice. One more thought: fallback policy when sidecar verification fails (e.g., control plane rejects token). We should have an automated retry with exponential backoff and a circuit-breaker that forces synchronous routing to old owner if retries exceed threshold.

maria: Agreed — add circuit-breaker and fail-fast policy in the control plane.

alex: Ok let's avoid coupling too tightly to compaction: make control-plane token issuance *aware* but not blocking on long compactions — reject only if compacted_until_seq is lagging by >M seconds. We'll tune M in canary.

lee: :thumbsup: I'll start a PR with bloom export + RPC batching. Jonathan, ping me when your probe is runnable so we can wire alerts.

sre-bot: Canary job queued: KC-2287-canary-run. Notifying on-call.

ops-bot: Reminder: include rollback instructions and config flags to disable sidecars in the PR for emergency rollback.
